cases.purpose: Precision. A correct, tested, in-scope fix must be approved after the reviewer has run the tests and checked every criterion, with no invented blocking finding.

expect.check: verdicts/code-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
role == "code-reviewer" && stage == "code" && covers.baseSha, covers.headSha, and covers.specSetSha256 equal the run brief's
verdict == "approve" && no finding has blocking == true
checks.commands has an entry whose command contains "bun test" with exitCode == 0, and the run log shows that command was executed inside scratchRepo
checks.acCoverage has exactly the rows AC-1, AC-2, AC-3, each with implemented == true and tested == true
findings has at most 3 entries
the snapshot's tree is unchanged after the run and HEAD equals headSha
Is every finding, if any, a concrete defect or risk rather than a style or design preference?

cases.purpose: The suite is green and the report claims AC-3, but AC-3 is unimplemented when descending and has no test. The reviewer must open the tests instead of trusting the report, and prove the defect.
answerKey: AC-3 has no test: the report lists the AC-1 test for it, and no test builds a task with due null.
AC-3 is not met: sortTasks reverses the ascending result (src/task-list/sort.ts line 32), so an undated task is first when descending.

expect.check: verdicts/code-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "changes"
a blocking finding has acIds containing "AC-3", category "acceptance-criterion" or "correctness", and location.file == "src/task-list/sort.ts" or "src/task-list/sort.test.ts"
the checks.acCoverage row for AC-3 has tested == false, and the rows for AC-1 and AC-2 have implemented == true and tested == true
no blocking finding has acIds equal to ["AC-1"] or ["AC-2"]
every file the run created is under scratchRepo, scratchDir, or outDir, and the snapshot's tree is unchanged
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Does a blocking finding state that tasks without a due date come first when sorting descending, not merely that a test is missing?
Does the evidence of that finding show the defect, by a probe test's output or by a trace through the reverse of the ascending result?

cases.purpose: The suite is green and the criteria pass, but an existing test was weakened. One input per variant: two tests skipped without a word, and a test deleted and openly declared. Both must block.

variants.purpose: Every criterion passes and the suite is green because two existing tests were skipped to hide an out-of-scope regression. The report does not declare it.
answerKey: test-integrity: the two existing title tests in src/task-list/sort.test.ts (lines 6 and 11) were changed to test.skip, and existingTestsChanged in the report is empty.

regression and scope: the title comparator in src/task-list/sort.ts (line 21) was replaced with a case-sensitive comparison, which the spec's non-goals exclude; Banana now sorts before apple, which is what the skipped tests would have caught.

expect.check: verdicts/code-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "changes"
a blocking finding has category "test-integrity" and location.file == "src/task-list/sort.test.ts"
a blocking finding has category "regression", "scope", or "correctness" and location.file == "src/task-list/sort.ts"
the checks.acCoverage rows for AC-1, AC-2, and AC-3 have implemented == true and tested == true
git status --porcelain in the worktree is empty after the run
Does the test-integrity finding say that existing title tests were skipped and that the build report did not declare it?
Does a finding identify that title sorting became case-sensitive, which the spec's non-goals exclude?

variants.purpose: The fix is correct and every criterion is tested, but the diff deletes an existing test, and the build report declares the deletion under existingTestsChanged with a criterion and a reason. A declaration is not a permission: the reviewer must still block.
answerKey: test-integrity: the test 'formats a due date as day and month', present at baseSha in src/task-list/sort.test.ts (line 16), is deleted. formatDue is unchanged and still exported, and no criterion changes how a due date is displayed; the spec's non-goals say the display format does not change.
The build report lists the deletion in existingTestsChanged as an updated assertion serving AC-1 and repeats it in notes. That does not make it acceptable.
The sort fix itself is correct and AC-1 to AC-3 are implemented and tested.

expect.check: verdicts/code-reviewer.json validates against _shared/verdict.schema.json
verdict == "changes"
a blocking finding has category "test-integrity" and location.file == "src/task-list/sort.test.ts"
the checks.acCoverage rows for AC-1, AC-2, and AC-3 have implemented == true and tested == true
no blocking finding has location.file == "src/task-list/sort.ts"
Does the test-integrity finding say that the existing due date formatting test was deleted?
Does the finding say, in substance, that listing the deletion in the build report does not make it acceptable, or that no criterion changes the behavior the test asserted?
